item.title: Paris Motor Show highlights deepening China-Europe auto cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
In the view of Serge Gachot, director of the Paris Motor Show, Chinese and European automakers have broad prospects for cooperation. He encouraged Chinese companies to invest in local production, research and development and supply chains. PARIS, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The ongoing 2026 Paris Motor Show not only features cutting-edge innovations in the auto industry, but also highlights growing opportunities for Chinese and European automakers to deepen cooperation. The week-long event, which opened on Oct. 12, brings together around 100 exhibitors and more than 60 automotive brands. A total of 25 Chinese brands, represented by 16 automakers including BYD, XPeng, Changan, Dongfeng and Leapmotor, are taking part in the show, setting a new record for Chinese participation. Serge Gachot, director of the Paris Motor Show, said that more Chinese automakers are placing greater emphasis on raising brand awareness while stepping up efforts to seek local partners, demonstrating a stronger commitment to the French and broader European markets. At the Stellantis exhibition area, Chinese automaker Leapmotor showcased its vehicles alongside European brands including Citroen and Peugeot. Leapmotor unveiled its new A05 electric compact car and flagship D19 SUV, while announcing that its B10 electric SUV had entered production at the Zaragoza plant in Spain. Developed in partnership with Stellantis and leveraging the European group's existing manufacturing infrastructure, the plant produces vehicles for the European market, marking an expansion of bilateral cooperation from sales to local manufacturing. Francesco Giacalone, head of product and marketing for Leapmotor International, said the Chinese automaker's brands complemented those of Stellantis, helping the European group reach a broader customer base and expand its market presence. Geely Automobile Holdings Limited made its first joint appearance at the show with its three brands: Geely, Lynk & Co and Zeekr. Nan Shengliang, vice president of Geely Auto Group and general manager of Geely Auto International Corporation, said the brand had entered 27 European countries and established more than 450 dealerships. In July, Geely Automobile Holdings and Ford Motor Company announced an agreement to produce new energy vehicles for the European market at Ford's manufacturing plant in Valencia, Spain. The arrangement is expected to help Geely accelerate its localization efforts while improving capacity utilization and supporting local employment. Marc Debord, head of communications at Volvo Car France, said that since Geely acquired Volvo Cars from Ford in 2010, sustained investment had helped Volvo accelerate the development of new platforms and powertrains, its transition to electrification and the expansion of its global business. The growing presence of Chinese automakers in Europe is also creating new opportunities for local auto parts suppliers. Francois Marion, chief communications and sustainability officer at French automotive supplier Valeo, said the company's European factories could supply components to Chinese automakers' vehicle production facilities in Europe as they expand their manufacturing footprint on the continent. Marion added that Valeo's research and development teams in China could work directly with Chinese automakers, further strengthening links between the Chinese and European automotive supply chains. Advanced driving technologies also took center stage at the show, with demonstrations extending beyond exhibition halls to the streets of Paris. XPeng and Tesla offer public test drives during the event. XPeng's Navigation Guided Pilot system has attracted interest and drawn many sign-ups for public rides. "The future of the automotive industry lies in software and artificial intelligence," said Thomas Rodier, head of marketing and communications at XPeng France. Chinese automakers' technological capabilities in these fields could also help European manufacturers accelerate their transformation, he added. In Gachot's view, Chinese and European automakers have broad prospects for cooperation. He encouraged Chinese companies to invest in local production, research and development and supply chains. Such investments would bring Chinese automakers more directly into Europe's automotive ecosystem, strengthening competition while creating further opportunities for cooperation, he said.■

item.title: Long March legacy takes root in greener landscapes of revolutionary heartlands
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Perched on a hillside in Changting County of southern China, visitors soak in lush scenery stretching beside the glistening Tingjiang River. But things weren't always so picturesque. Changting, an old revolutionary base area in Fujian Province, was among the counties hardest hit by soil erosion in China's red-soil region, which threatened local people's livelihoods and left the landscape degraded. Efforts to improve the local environment began nearly a century ago. In November 1931, the Communist Party of China (CPC) established the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic in Ruijin, Jiangxi Province, where the CPC put its revolutionary ideals into governance experimentation. The following year, it launched a tree-planting campaign to protect farmland from floods and droughts, reclaim barren hills and benefit local people. During this campaign, CPC-led Red Army soldiers in Changting, which neighbors Ruijin, taught residents how to plant trees. In turn, residents brought food and seedlings to the soldiers and joined the planting campaign voluntarily. "Even amid the turmoil of war, the Party still called for tree planting with great vigor," said Chen Liping, a researcher of CPC history and local chronicles in the county. "It reflects the Party's commitment to putting people's interests first and laying the foundations for future development." As the war intensified, however, the tree-planting campaign had to be halted. The Red Army then embarked on the Long March, an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936 that broke through the encirclement of Kuomintang (Nationalist Party) forces. With some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers, the arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. As one of the starting points of the Long March, Changting has carried forward the Red Army's legacy in its decades-long efforts to combat soil erosion. Tree planting, as the Red Army had practiced earlier, remained an effective method to tackle the problem. However, in severely eroded areas, ground temperatures can soar above 70 degrees Celsius, making it difficult for trees to survive. Through experimentation, the county developed a phased approach suited to its natural conditions: first planting grass, then shrubs, and next trees, bringing the barren hills back to life step by step. "Grass helps lower ground temperatures and create favorable conditions for other vegetation, allowing a mix of tree species to take root," said Shangguan Yuanbin, deputy head of the county's soil and water conservation station. Over the years, local people adapted to changing conditions and met emerging problems with determination, patience and ingenuity. Years of effort have paid off. To date, Changting has reduced the area affected by soil erosion by about 1.17 million mu (about 78,000 hectares), while its soil erosion rate fell from 31.47 percent to 6.31 percent, according to local authorities. "Had we given up at any point over these decades, we would not have achieved such results today," said Shangguan. "We've applied the fearless Long March spirit to soil and water conservation." Changting's transformation epitomizes a broader greening trend in China, which marks a national tree-planting day annually. Official data showed that between 2021 and 2025, China accounted for roughly one-quarter of the world's increase in green vegetation, while its forest and grass coverage rate exceeded 56 percent in 2025. China's greening endeavor has gained international recognition. In 2021, Changting's comprehensive soil erosion control and ecological restoration practices were selected as a model case at the 15th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP15). But restoring the land is not the end of the story. The next challenge is to turn environmental recovery into lasting economic opportunities for local communities. One of these places is Xikuangshan, an old mining area in central China's Hunan Province. During the Long March, about 1,500 well-disciplined Red Army soldiers were stationed there for a week. Through their words and deeds, they gained the trust of locals, who went from hiding from the Red Army to following it. Dubbed the "World's Capital of Antimony," Xikuangshan has witnessed decades of intensive underground mining dating back to 1897, which led to vegetation loss, air and water pollution, and ground subsidence. Some even joked that "a white bird flying across Xikuangshan could turn black." In 2004, local people mounted an all-out campaign for ecological restoration. Inspired by the perseverance shown by the Red Army, a research team conducted countless experiments and finally achieved a breakthrough in the treatment of harmful residue generated during antimony refining, a challenge that has long confronted the industry worldwide. The once-scarred mining landscape gradually regained its vitality. The improved environment, together with its revolutionary history and mining culture, helped Xikuangshan to develop into a well-known tourist destination with around 300 million yuan (about 44.6 million U.S. dollars) in tourism revenue annually. Yang Lijun is among those who have benefited. After more than a decade, he decided to return home in 2021 upon seeing his hometown's blue skies and clear waters. He rented an abandoned rural house and opened a tourist restaurant featuring local specialties, which now generates an annual income of more than 100,000 yuan. "In the past, many residents, myself included, left home because of worsening environmental conditions," he recalled. "Now, with the environment improving, more tourists are coming, bringing new opportunities for a better life." For places like Changting and Xikuangshan, ecological restoration is therefore not simply about bringing back greenery, but also about higher-quality lives and new development paths for former revolutionary base areas. Earlier this year, China issued guidelines on accelerating the development of such areas, with measures to support systematic environmental protection and encourage eco-tourism. For Yue Hui, director of the soil and water conservation center in Changting, the changes are encouraging, but the work is far from over. "Combating soil erosion requires sustained effort. We will continue our march toward a greener future," Yue said. ■

item.title: Why has "China Haul" become new buzzword on social media worldwide?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Foreign tourists buy handheld camera equipment at a flagship store of DJI in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, June 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) By Liu He More and more foreign visitors are arriving in China with empty suitcases and returning home with bags full of Chinese goods. What is behind this trend? British YouTuber Elliot Page offered a glimpse of the appeal with a shopping vlog filmed in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province. Exploring Chinese sportswear brands such as Li-Ning and Anta, Page was impressed not only by their affordability, but also by their design and quality. Sportswear is just the tip of the iceberg. As "China Haul" gains traction on social media worldwide, an increasing number of international visitors are traveling to China not only to explore its attractions, but also to discover and shop for products that catch their eye. In the first seven months of 2026, people from overseas spent 263.6 billion yuan (about 39 billion U.S. dollars) in China, an increase of 27.8 percent year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. What is drawing international consumers to Chinese goods? The growing appeal of homegrown Chinese brands is giving international consumers more reasons to take notice. "Chinese products, like clothes, accessories and daily necessities, are not only competitively priced, but also feature trendy designs that are hard to find in stores in my home country," said Carlos Alvarado, an international student from Guatemala, now a seasoned shopper in China. An increasingly visitor-friendly shopping environment is making it easier for international tourists to spend in China. Visa-free entry arrangements and expanded departure tax refund services have further enhanced the country's appeal as a shopping destination. From sprawling shopping malls and efficient delivery services to delivery robots that bring orders right to hotel doors, China offers a seamless shopping experience that lowers the barriers for foreign visitors. "Foreign tourists now account for 30 percent of our daily customer flow," said Zhou Man, manager of a Xiaomi store in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province. Chinese cultural products are broadening the appeal of shopping in China, giving visitors more opportunities to connect purchases with the stories and creativity behind them. From globally popular designer toys such as Labubu to the animated blockbuster Ne Zha 2, Chinese cultural products are capturing international attention. As international audiences become more familiar with Chinese cultural creations, shopping in China can offer another way to discover the country's contemporary culture and everyday life. China Haul, at its core, reflects a simple shift: foreign visitors are discovering China's global appeal firsthand, exploring its products and brands for themselves rather than relying on secondhand impressions. By sharing their shopping finds online, they are introducing the world to a more diverse and appealing side of China.

item.title: Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen named among FAO's 100 women heroes
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu said women are a driving force in agrifood systems, playing an indispensable role in food security, natural resource management, rural development and community resilience. ROME, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen has been named among the FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, a global recognition initiative launched by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The honorees were celebrated at a ceremony on Thursday at the FAO headquarters in Rome as part of this year's World Food Forum. Yin has spent more than four decades combating desertification in the Maowusu Sandy Land in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. After decades of persistent tree planting, she and her family have transformed stretches of the once-barren landscape into a green expanse, overcoming harsh conditions and shifting sands. Her story also forged an enduring friendship with retired U.S. teacher Ronald Sakolsky, who raised 5,000 U.S. dollars decades ago to support her afforestation work. Yin told Xinhua that the recognition had strengthened her resolve to continue her work. "Like a Mongolian horse, I will keep pressing forward with perseverance and determination, doing my work well and giving back to nature," she said. Sitting in the audience, Sakolsky's eyes grew moist as he applauded Yin's achievement. "Yin deserves everything that she gets. She is the heroine," he told Xinhua. Addressing the ceremony, FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu hailed women farmers' roles. He said women are a driving force in agrifood systems, playing an indispensable role in food security, natural resource management, rural development and community resilience. Qu then invited Sakolsky to join Yin on stage. The two friends embraced once again and held up a trophy together. Qu said that although Sakolsky was not among the women heroes, his "passion" and "solidarity" should be recognized. Sakolsky expressed his gratitude, saying he was deeply moved by Yin's remarkable achievement. He called on everyone to plant a tree and work together to make a difference to the environment. Launched by the FAO to mark the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026, the global initiative recognizes 100 women for their outstanding contributions to agriculture, food systems and rural development. The FAO said it received 609 nominations from 131 members. The selection process involved an eligibility review, an assessment, and ranking by senior management, and two rounds of deliberations. Besides Yin, Yu Jinxiu and Dong Minfang were also among the FAO 100 Women Heroes. Yu is a moxibustion therapist from Qichun County in central China's Hubei Province, and Dong is president of the Fengrui Agricultural Machinery Professional Cooperative in Yueyang County, central China's Hunan Province. They have spent years sharing their expertise to help thousands of people secure jobs and start businesses, raising incomes for rural residents. The United Nations designated 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer to highlight women's contribution to agrifood systems and promote policies and investments that improve their access to finance, knowledge and services.

item.title: China's R&D spending up 8.2 pct in 2025
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- China's research and development (R&D) expenditure rose 8.2 percent year on year to 3.93 trillion yuan (about 584.5 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said on Friday. Over the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), the country's R&D spending rose at an average annual rate of 10 percent, making China the world's second-largest R&D investor, said Luo Qiushi, an NBS statistician. China's R&D intensity, which measures spending as a share of GDP, rose 0.11 percentage points to 2.8 percent last year, exceeding the OECD average of 2.72 percent for the first time and ranking 12th in the world. By type of R&D activity, spending on basic research, applied research and experimental development grew 13.3 percent, 3.2 percent and 8.4 percent year on year to 283.46 billion yuan, 444.16 billion yuan and 3.2 trillion yuan, respectively. Enterprise R&D spending exceeded 3 trillion yuan for the first time, accounting for 77.4 percent of the total. Enterprises have accounted for more than 77 percent of the country's total R&D spending for four consecutive years, and their contribution to the overall increase reached 73.7 percent, cementing their role as the main engine of China's R&D spending expansion, according to the NBS. ■

item.title: China to host global governance forum from Oct. 23 to 25
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- China will host the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) from Oct. 23 to 25 in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province, according to the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs (CPIFA). The forum will bring together leading figures in strategic, political, academic, business, media, and youth sectors from around the world, particularly those in areas such as the United Nations, climate change, artificial intelligence, and multilateral trade, said the CPIFA at a press conference on Friday. According to the CPIFA, international guests from nearly 100 countries of the Global South, Europe and America have confirmed their attendance. They will also visit Xiongan New Area, China's "city of the future," during the forum. Hosted by the CPIFA, the forum is themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World." ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Hunan University on its centenary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday extended congratulations to faculty, students and alumni of Hunan University as it marks its 100th anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a congratulatory letter to the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward fine revolutionary traditions, continue to elevate the quality and levels of its teaching, and strive to nurture more talent who can apply their knowledge to practical affairs, so as to make new contributions to building China into an education powerhouse and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1926, Hunan University has nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent over the past century. ■

item.title: 70 years on, China's Canton Fair highlights innovation, intelligence in global trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
GUANGZHOU, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, opened to visitors in Guangzhou, capital of south China's Guangdong Province on Thursday, with more than 30,000 exhibiting companies and about 340,000 overseas buyers expected to attend. Serving as a barometer and wind vane of China's foreign trade, this year's fair, marking its 70th anniversary, features innovation, intelligence, greater specialization and higher quality. The Canton Fair is one of the world's few one-stop trade platforms offering a complete range of products with convenience and efficiency, while bringing together the latest products and technologies. About 64 percent of exhibitors apply new technologies such as the industrial internet and artificial intelligence (AI). New and green products account for 23.2 percent and 26 percent of the exhibits, respectively, with both hitting record highs, and more than 700 new-product launch events will be held. The fair has further enhanced its digital and intelligent operations, introducing 22 smart application scenarios and 16 AI applications for the first time, while booth navigation now covers the entire venue. "We have always worked together with exhibitors and buyers to jointly uphold the multilateral trading system and promote the building of an open world economy," said Zhu Yong, director of the China Foreign Trade Center. The 140th Canton Fair runs in three phases in Guangzhou from Oct. 15 to Nov. 4. Over the past 70 years, the Canton Fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade event, with the most complete product range, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. ■

item.title: Beijing forum discusses counter-terrorism challenges posed by intelligent technologies
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
Participants communicate with each other during the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 14, 2026. The Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism concluded here on Thursday. (Photo by Yue Chang/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism concluded in Beijing on Thursday, with more than 320 experts and frontline personnel from 62 countries and international organizations discussing counter-terrorism challenges, including those arising from advances in unmanned and intelligent technologies. During the three-day forum, participants discussed the terrorism situation, explored solutions to common challenges, exchanged practical experience and explored avenues for international cooperation. Participants noted that the rapid development of unmanned and intelligent technologies has made terrorist activities increasingly covert and destructive, as new methods are adopted to carry out acts of terrorism and violence. They said traditional approaches that rely on individual countries acting alone and isolated prevention and control measures are increasingly inadequate to address emerging terrorist threats that are transnational, covert and enabled by intelligent technologies. The participants said combating terrorism requires countries to keep pace with advances in unmanned and intelligent technologies, strengthen their counter-terrorism capabilities, and work together to establish and improve international cooperation mechanisms for preventing and combating terrorism. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the Great Wall forum. Since its launch in 2016, the Chinese People's Armed Police Force has hosted six editions of the forum. This year's event focused on changing circumstances, evolving adversaries and technological advances, and examined the impact of artificial intelligence on efforts to prevent and combat terrorism. Discussions were organized into high-level, professional and thematic forums, creating a comprehensive, multilevel dialogue platform spanning the strategic, operational and tactical levels. An important participant in and contributor to the global fight against terrorism, China has engaged in pragmatic cooperation with other countries in terms of intelligence exchanges, border control, case investigations and counter-terrorism financing. It has also organized training sessions and seminars to share its experience with the international community and help strengthen counter-terrorism capabilities. ■ A participant interacts with a robot during the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 14, 2026.
